data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A test constrains its subject only if the test's failure conditions are independent of the subject's own validation logic; otherwise the test describes a tautology, and the 1/9 loss occurs because compile.py's shown-to-fail-first installation accidentally aligns the test's failure with the subject's self-validation.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If compile.py's mutation operators cannot distinguish self-validation from independent assertion, the 1/9 loss is an instrumentation limit, not a description/constraint distinction.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the ordinarily-guarded modules' 4/4 to 6/7 rates arise from guard diversity rather than test independence, the tautology claim fails.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the lost mutation was in a code path not executed by any test, the loss is a coverage gap, not a description relation.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"When a test imports the same validation checker the subject uses, the test's verdict is derived from the subject's own verdict function. Under shown-to-fail-first installation, the planted mutation fails the subject's self-check, so the test reports the failure, but this is description (restating the subject's self-report) rather than constraint. The 3-of-26 result distribution shows that only mutations escaping the subject's self-check are true constraints; the 1/9 lost mutation was one such escape that compile.py's installation order masked.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
